newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak govt discusses new c.bank board member.
newsitem.headline: Slovak govt discusses new c.bank board member.

text.p: The Slovak government said it will discuss the appointment of a new central bank governing board member at its regular Tuesday session.
National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) governor Vladimir Masar will present the proposal, which was added to the original agenda, a government statement said. The statement gave no further details.
Three of the eight seats on the governing board are vacant and are the subject of talks with the government.
Local bankers have been watching the talks amid growing concern that any new board member the government appoints could lead to less NBS independence and easier monetary policy.

Leading government officials have repeatedly criticised the NBS's tight monetary policy, which was further tightened at the end of 1996 after the government approved a fiscal deficit of 3.7 percent of GDP for this year, compared with a 0.4-percent surplus in 1996.

Last week, the Slovak official news agency TASR said Jozef Magula, the former deputy finance minister who was replaced at the previous government's session, "would (probably) take a high function in the NBS."
